entries.headline: Red Canyon Resources closes $745,000 flow-through raise for BC critical minerals
entries.dek: The non-brokered placement issued 3,725,000 flow-through units at $0.20 each, with half-warrants exercisable at $0.30 for 18 months.
entries.caption: A drill rig stands idle at first light as Red Canyon Resources closes a flow-through financing in British Columbia.
unverified_claims: The characterization of the use of proceeds as qualifying 'flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures,' and the stated renunciation and expenditure deadlines, rest solely on the company's own release.
brief: Red Canyon Resources Ltd. (CSE: REDC) (OTCQB: REDRF) has closed a non-brokered flow-through private placement, raising gross proceeds of $745,000 through 3,725,000 flow-through units priced at $0.20 each. Each unit includes one flow-through common share and one-half of one warrant, with each whole warrant exercisable at $0.30 for 18 months.

The company said the flow-through proceeds will fund Canadian exploration expenditures that qualify as flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures on its Kendal and Osiris projects and other eligible British Columbia properties, with an expenditure deadline of December 31, 2027 and renunciation effective December 31, 2026. The company paid $24,025 in finder's fees, and insiders purchased 937,500 of the units.

All securities issued under the offering are restricted from trading until February 27, 2027, and the financing closed October 26, 2026, the company said, giving Red Canyon fresh capital to advance exploration on its British Columbia projects.
body: Red Canyon Resources Ltd. (CSE: REDC) (OTCQB: REDRF) (Frankfurt: I91) has closed a non-brokered flow-through private placement for gross proceeds of $745,000. The offering consisted of 3,725,000 flow-through units priced at $0.20 each. Each FT Unit comprised one flow-through common share and one-half of one common share purchase warrant, with each whole warrant exercisable into one common share at $0.30 for an 18-month term.

A flow-through share lets the company renounce the associated Canadian exploration expenses to the subscriber, who can then claim them against their own income for tax purposes — which is why flow-through financings are typically priced at a premium to a company's regular shares. Red Canyon's release did not state whether this placement carried that kind of premium.

The company said the proceeds qualify as flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures and are earmarked for exploration on its Kendal and Osiris projects and other eligible British Columbia properties. The expenditure deadline is December 31, 2027, and the related renunciation of the expenses to subscribers is effective December 31, 2026, the company said.

Red Canyon paid finder's fees of $24,025 in connection with the offering. Insiders of the company purchased 937,500 of the flow-through units, the release said, without further detail on which insiders participated or in what amounts individually.
All securities issued under the offering — the flow-through shares and the warrants — are restricted from trading until February 27, 2027. The offering closed October 26, 2026.

Red Canyon is a Vancouver-based company exploring in British Columbia, trading on the CSE under REDC, on the OTCQB under REDRF, and in Frankfurt under I91. The release did not disclose the current size of the company's exploration programs beyond naming the Kendal and Osiris projects as a focus for the new proceeds.

entries.headline: MineHub arranges $1.5 million placement, pushes warrant expiry out to 2027
entries.dek: The non-brokered financing prices units at $0.40 with $0.55 warrants, while more than 15.7 million existing warrants get an eleven-month extension.
entries.caption: A dim server room corridor stands quiet as MineHub Technologies arranges a private placement to shore up working capital.

sources.title: MineHub Technologies Inc.: MineHub Announces Financing
MineHub Technologies Launches $1.5 Million Non-Brokered Private Placement and Extends Warrants to 2027

unverified_claims: The stated use of proceeds — working capital and 'continuing to evaluate strategic, corporate and financial opportunities' — and the insider-participation disclosure rest solely on the company's own release.
brief: MineHub Technologies Inc. (TSXV: MHUB) (OTCQB: MHUBF) has arranged a non-brokered private placement to raise up to CAD $1,500,000. The offering consists of up to 3,750,000 units at $0.40 each, with each unit made up of one common share and half of one warrant exercisable at $0.55 for two years from closing.

The company is also extending 15,760,417 previously issued warrants — exercisable at $0.40 and $0.50 — to a new expiry of December 31, 2027, from January 31, 2027. Certain insiders may participate in the placement, which is subject to TSX Venture Exchange approval and relies on exemptions from formal valuation and shareholder-approval requirements.

MineHub says the proceeds will go to working capital and to continue evaluating strategic, corporate and financial opportunities, as the Vancouver-based digital commodity supply chain company awaits exchange sign-off on the offering.
body: MineHub Technologies Inc. (TSXV: MHUB) (OTCQB: MHUBF) has arranged a non-brokered private placement to raise up to CAD $1,500,000. The offering consists of up to 3,750,000 units priced at $0.40 each. Each unit is made up of one common share and one-half of one transferable common share purchase warrant, with each whole warrant exercisable at $0.55 per common share for two years from the closing date.

A unit, in this structure, bundles a share together with the right to buy additional shares later at a fixed price — the warrant — giving subscribers upside if the stock trades above $0.55 before the warrant expires, without requiring them to pay for that right up front beyond the unit price.

Alongside the new placement, MineHub is extending the expiry of warrants it issued earlier. Prior warrants covering 14,584,954 shares at an exercise price of $0.40, issued January 31, 2024, along with 625,000 warrants at $0.50 issued July 25, 2025 and 550,463 warrants at $0.50 issued August 20, 2025, all had their expiry pushed from January 31, 2027 to December 31, 2027.

The company said certain insiders of MineHub may participate in the new placement, relying on exemptions from the formal valuation and minority shareholder approval requirements that would otherwise apply to insider participation under Multilateral Instrument 61-101.
Closing of the offering is subject to the company's receipt of TSX Venture Exchange approval, MineHub said. No closing date was given in the release.

MineHub said the proceeds are earmarked for working capital and for continuing to evaluate strategic, corporate and financial opportunities. The release gave no further detail on what those opportunities might involve.

body: Nvidia is investing $3 billion in Meta Platforms' equity offering, which Meta increased to $97.5 billion. Reuters reported the enlarged raise is the largest fundraising in Meta's history. Meta is raising the money as it accelerates investment in AI infrastructure, Reuters reported.

The deal deepens an existing partnership on Muse, Meta's personal AI assistant, internally known as Hatch, which runs on Nvidia infrastructure. Muse can access a user's email, calendar, payments, health, shopping and smart-home applications, with users able to revoke that access at any time, according to the reporting.
The companies are also exploring joint work on Nvidia's OpenShell framework and a monitoring tool called Sentry, which is intended to track AI agent behaviour, Reuters reported.

Chief executive Mark Zuckerberg has described Muse as central to delivering what he calls "personal superintelligence" to Meta's users; the system is modelled on the open-source AI agent OpenClaw, according to the reporting.

On the venture boards, the news coincided with trading in the artificial-intelligence theme, a group of 29 listed names of which 19 traded today. The group's median move was 0.00%, against +0.53% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of 0.53 percentage points below the broader junior index.

Three of the larger movers were Sparc AI Inc. (CSE: SPAI), which rose 36.90% to CAD2.3; Yocale.ai Inc. (CSE: YAI), which rose 1.33% to CAD0.76; and Railtown AI Technologies Inc. (CSE: RAIL), which was unchanged at CAD0.28. Each is in the theme because its registered name contains "ai".

Nothing ties these moves to the Nvidia-Meta announcement; the two events fall on the same trading day, and the venture board's theme, taken as a whole, underperformed the broader Venture Composite rather than outperforming it.

entries.headline: Anthropic files for an IPO that could be the biggest ever
entries.dek: The AI company could raise up to $100 billion at a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion, even as its chief executive warns of a risk to humanity from unchecked AI.
entries.caption: A trading floor sits quiet before the bell as Anthropic prepares what could be the largest IPO on record.

sources.title: Anthropic files for potentially the biggest IPO ever as CEO warns of risk to humanity from AI
Anthropic files for potentially biggest IPO ever as CEO warns of risk to humanity from AI

unverified_claims: The $100 billion potential raise and $1.5-2 trillion valuation range, the founders' projected 1.4% stakes and $28 billion potential individual wealth, and Dario Amodei's warning that AI could let loose "a swarm of agents" that could "take over the entire internet" within six to 12 months rest on reporting of the company's filing and statements, not on figures independently confirmed by this publication.
brief: Anthropic has filed for an initial public offering that could be the largest ever, potentially raising as much as $100 billion and valuing the San Francisco company at $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion, according to the Associated Press. The company plans to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT.

Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI staff including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, Anthropic reported more than $16 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026, fourteen times a year earlier, alongside a net loss of $80.7 billion that includes a $72.4 billion one-time accounting charge. Its founders will retain 50.1% voting control through a special share class.

None of the two listed venture names in the space theme cleared the liquidity floor required to be named today, so no junior move is reported alongside this story. The theme's venture board accordingly offers nothing to set against Anthropic's filing today.
body: Anthropic has filed papers for an initial public offering that could be the largest in history, the Associated Press reported. The filing sets up a Wall Street debut as soon as next month, with the company potentially raising as much as $100 billion at a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion — topping the $86 billion raised by SpaceX's IPO in June, previously the record.

Anthropic plans to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT. The company was founded in 2021 by a group of former OpenAI employees, including siblings Dario Amodei, its chief executive, and Daniela Amodei, its president. It reported revenue of more than $16 billion for the first half of 2026, fourteen times the prior year's figure, according to the AP.

Anthropic also reported a net loss of $80.7 billion for the period, which includes a one-time accounting charge of $72.4 billion. The company has not yet reported a profit. Its seven founders are each expected to hold about 1.4% of the company, a stake that could be worth as much as $28 billion apiece at the top of the expected valuation range, the AP reported.

The founders will retain 50.1% voting control through a special class of shares, and the company has established a Long-Term Benefit Trust of independent directors with the power to appoint board members, structured to keep financial interests from overriding public-safety considerations, according to the filing as reported by the AP.

Dario Amodei has separately argued, in a post on his website, for slowing development of the most advanced AI models, warning that without an industry slowdown, AI could let loose "a swarm of agents" that could "take over the entire internet" within six to 12 months, the AP reported.

The space theme on this publication's venture boards comprises two listed names; neither cleared the C$25,000 daily-volume floor this publication requires before naming a security today. No junior move is therefore reported alongside Anthropic's filing, and no names are given.

entries.headline: US and Canada edge toward a deal to ease steel and auto tariffs
entries.dek: Talks center on Section 232 duties of up to 50% on steel and 25% on autos, with Canadian sources saying a deal before the November 3 elections is possible but would likely be narrower in scope.

sources.title: Exclusive-US, Canada working on deal to ease steel, auto tariffs, sources say

unverified_claims: The characterization of the talks as 'constructive dialogue' by a spokesperson for LeBlanc, the 'slight intensification' described by Prime Minister Carney, and the Canadian sources' separate predictions about the timing and likely scope of a deal rest on sources and quotes relayed by Reuters and are not independently confirmed by this publication.
brief: The United States and Canada are working on a deal to ease U.S. tariffs on Canadian steel and autos, Reuters reported, citing sources close to the talks. The negotiations follow the collapse of broader trade talks in August and focus on Section 232 duties of up to 50% on steel and 25% on autos.

U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Canada's Dominic LeBlanc have been in regular contact, Reuters reported. Trump has said he would raise Canadian steel tariffs to 50% from January 1, 2027, absent a deal, and predicted at a rally that the dispute would be resolved "soon." One Canadian source said a deal was possible before the November 3 elections, while a separate source said any deal was likely to be narrower in scope.

No venture-market name in the tariffs theme traded today, so this publication reports no group measure and names nobody; the theme simply produced no trading today to compare against the broader board.
body: The United States and Canada are working on a deal to ease U.S. tariffs on Canadian steel and autos, Reuters reported, citing sources briefed on the talks. The negotiations aim to repair relations that soured after broader trade talks broke down in August, and focus on Section 232 duties — a US trade-law provision under which Washington has imposed tariffs of up to 50% on Canadian steel and 25% on Canadian autos.

Trump has said he intends to raise the Canadian steel tariff to 50% from its current level starting January 1, 2027, absent a deal. He predicted at a political rally on Sunday that the trade dispute would be resolved "soon," without giving specifics, Reuters reported.

Because Section 232 tariffs are administered by the US Commerce Department, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is at the center of the talks rather than the Office of the US Trade Representative, and Reuters reported he has been in regular contact with Canada's Dominic LeBlanc, the minister handling the file for Ottawa.

A spokesperson for LeBlanc described the discussions as "constructive dialogue" on "a range of priorities." Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said there had been a "slight intensification" in talks, adding that "to the extent any progress has been made, it's because the US is coming closer to our position." One Canadian source briefed on the negotiations told Reuters that a deal was possible before the November 3 US midterm elections. A separate Canadian industry source told Reuters that any deal was likely to be "a narrowed deal" if it happens.
Trump signed an order on Friday removing the 50% tariff on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products, Reuters reported.

This publication's tariffs theme produced no trading today, so there is no junior read-through to set alongside the talks: no venture name in the theme traded, leaving no group measure and no names to report, unlike the artificial-intelligence and space themes tracked elsewhere in this issue.
